items.notes: Closes watch W-261025-04. Ukraine's Arakhamia wants the next round multilateral, with Europe.
items.text: The [[e:2026 United States–Ukraine–Russia meetings in Abu Dhabi|Abu Dhabi talks]] ended after two days with a large-scale prisoner exchange agreed but no breakthrough. [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]] cited mutual understanding on some issues; [[p:Jared Kushner]] said territory remains hardest but progress was made on a post-war security framework. TASS says the swap should come within two to three weeks. Kushner and [[p:Steve Witkoff]] arrived in Moscow on 12 Nov to brief Putin and will then debrief Zelenskyy in Dublin.

items.notes: Logged late (9 Nov letter, not in earlier logs). Separately, Council and Parliament agreed the 2027 annual budget on 11 Nov.
items.text: [[p:Friedrich Merz]] wrote to [[p:António Costa]] that Germany will block the 2028–34 EU budget unless all member states commit to multiyear Ukraine funding from 2028. Hungary, Slovakia, Bulgaria and the Czech Republic refuse more aid; Ukraine faces a roughly €70bn financing gap in 2027.

items.notes: Tanker fires are an IRGC claim; UKMTO separately reported a tanker hit by a projectile off Oman.
items.text: Iran's [[p:Mohsen Rezaei]] called reports of talks with Washington a lie, and [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] said Hormuz stays shut until US terms on sanctions, the blockade and all fronts are met, though a two-day reopening offer stands. The IRGC said three tankers were burning in the strait; ADNOC reported an attack on one of its vessels. [[p:Marco Rubio]] said the economic campaign makes major combat unnecessary.

Abiy's Horn adviser [[p:Getachew Reda]] told the UN Horn of Africa envoy that [[p:Isaias Afwerki]]'s Eritrea and [[p:Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]]'s Sudan arm groups inside Ethiopia, and blamed Sudan for drone attacks. Asmara and Khartoum did not respond in the report; Eritrea has denied backing Tigrayan rebels.

Trump named [[p:Stephen Miller (political advisor)|Stephen Miller]] White House chief of staff, replacing [[p:Susie Wiles]], who moves to his political operation; it is the most senior departure since the midterm defeat. Miller, the architect of the deportation drive, took over on 9 Nov.

The House voted 211–204 to send [[p:Thomas Massie]]'s resolution to impeach [[p:Pete Hegseth]] to committee, shelving it. Its eight articles centre on waging war on Iran without congressional authorization; Massie was the only Republican to break ranks, and [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] called it "just the beginning".

items.notes: Jordan–Scalise tally is from sources cited by CBS.
items.text: House Republicans picked [[p:Jim Jordan]] as their next leader, beating [[p:Steve Scalise]] 106–73 by sources' count; [[p:John Thune]] stays Senate Republican leader. On the Democratic side, [[p:Bernie Sanders]] says he won't back [[p:Chuck Schumer]] for majority leader; Democrats vote next month.

Congress returned for its lame-duck session facing an 11 Dec funding deadline; a stopgap is likely. Some Democrats, including [[p:Ro Khanna]] and Schumer, want to use the funding fight to restrict the [[e:2026 Iran war|Iran war]], and the defence authorization bill remains blocked over the war.

items.notes: CNBC figure from headline (page not reachable); KCRA gave ~2,500 on 7 Nov and ~30,000 ballots outstanding. 56-seat total assumes 54 already won. Watch W-261105-02.
items.text: The Alaska and Mississippi Senate races remain uncalled, with Democrats ahead: [[p:Scott Colom]] led [[p:Cindy Hyde-Smith]] by more than 4,400 votes and [[p:Mary Peltola]] widened her lead over [[p:Dan Sullivan (American senator)|Dan Sullivan]]. Wins in both would give Democrats 56 seats.

[[p:Mark Carney]] said the White House, not the new Congress, will decide trade deals for the next two or three years. He says Washington has dropped demands on Canadian culture, French-language protections and Canada's freedom to strike other deals, but tough issues remain under the 50% US tariffs. He will meet [[p:Xi Jinping]] at APEC.

[[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]] confirmed a bilateral meeting with Xi during APEC (she travels 15–20 Nov) and wants to see Trump if he attends. She said ties with Washington are unchanged under the new chief of staff and kept her opposition to labelling cartels as terrorist organizations.

items.notes: Foro Penal counted 322 political prisoners as of 26 Oct (via Radio América VE).
items.text: [[p:María Corina Machado]] endorsed the US State Department's phased roadmap in a message to the Ibero-American summit in Madrid: renew the supreme court by end-2026, then a new electoral council, after which [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]] declares the presidency vacant and calls elections within six months.

items.notes: Blackouts continue; the UNE forecast about 1,960 MW of shortfall at peak on 10 Nov.
items.text: The State Department sanctioned eight companies and two people, including China's state-owned CEIEC, for moving oil to Cuba or arming its military, and blocked five tankers; OFAC opened Cuba's electronics, technology and maritime sectors to sanctions. Foreign Minister [[p:Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla|Bruno Rodríguez]] then flew to Beijing seeking support.

items.notes: Death toll unconfirmed. Four Salvadoran GSF members missing since 18 Oct; no word they were found.
items.text: Haitian police backed by Salvadoran troops struck the headquarters of [[p:400 Mawozo]] in Croix-des-Bouquets; [[p:Nayib Bukele]] posted helicopter footage and about 20 people were reported killed. Amnesty International asked both governments to publish the deployment agreement. PM [[p:Alix Didier Fils-Aimé]] visits El Salvador next week to discuss the troops' future.

Ousted president [[p:Santiago Peña]] was arrested on 6 Nov and a judge ordered pretrial detention on 7 Nov over the Ueno Bank collapse, which involves about $355m of social-security funds; prosecutors say he faces up to 15 years. His successor [[p:Pedro Alliana]] asked all ministers to resign on 9 Nov.

President [[p:Abelardo de la Espriella]] authorized an eighth air strike on armed groups in three months, target not yet named; the seventh, on 9 Nov in Tibú, hit a FARC dissident front and killed four, the army says. Joint US–Colombian exercises with about 750 troops ended at Tolemaida.

items.notes: El Destape is opposition-leaning; crowd figure (3m) not used. Argentina also argued its Falklands oil case at ITLOS.
items.text: [[p:Pope Leo XIV]] closed his Argentina visit with a mass in Luján and calls for reconciliation after criticizing austerity; [[p:Javier Milei]] skipped the mass and saw him off at the airport, and his spokesman defended audits of disability pensions and universities. The CGT unions are planning a protest, and Torcuato Di Tella University puts urban poverty at 32.6%.
Pope Leo XIV, a naturalized Peruvian, began a 11–16 Nov visit with a welcome at the Government Palace in Lima, then goes to Chiclayo, Cajamarca, Cusco and Pucallpa.

Lula has not signalled his fourth-term cabinet; picks are expected in the second half of November. Finance could go to Alckmin, Haddad or incumbent Dario Durigan, and Senator Camilo Santana leads for chief of staff.
Federal Police opened an inquiry, ordered by Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino, into suspected foreign funding of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign; the campaign and Meta deny wrongdoing.
President Kast's approval fell to 24% in a Criteria poll, and the central bank's survey of economists projects zero growth for 2026; Kast has refused a cabinet reshuffle.

items.notes: Cuban state agency; dates match CNE campaign calendar.
items.text: The National Assembly granted Noboa leave to campaign for his party in the 29 Nov local elections (12–18 and 20–26 Nov); Vice-President María José Pinto acts as president.
As Rodrigo Paz marked a year in office, Vice-President Edmand Lara accused him of ordering a case built against him over leaked audio recordings.
